_policy: Every consciously deferred piece of work gets a row: what was deferred, why, what enforcement exists meanwhile, and a review-by date. `cargo xtask deferrals --check` (weekly scheduled CI) fails once a row passes its date un-re-decided — a deferral nobody re-examines is a silent forever. Re-deciding means either building the thing (delete the row) or re-dating it with a fresh reason in the same commit. Decisions intended to be permanent do not belong here; they get ADRs.

deferrals.what: The pinned suite's fourteen auth/* client scenarios (OAuth metadata discovery, registration, PKCE flows) as host-SUT gates
deferrals.why: Requires a full OAuth client; ADR-0009 §5 scoped it out of M3 exactly as the registry's TRAN-009 exclusion records for the server side
deferrals.meanwhile: TRAN-009 documented exclusion; the four protocol scenarios gate in CI

deferrals.what: Re-check DRAFT_SUITE_VERSION against the npm `alpha` dist-tag and bump it if it has moved, with a BLESS=1 re-measurement and a scenario diff review in the same commit
deferrals.why: New row 2026-08-18, opened by the failure it describes: the ratchet sat on 0.2.0-alpha.9 for six weeks while alpha.10 and alpha.11 shipped, and alpha.11 turned out to add a `wire-schema-valid` check that fails the 2025-11-25 leg on exactly the clause (CACH-001, missing ttlMs/cacheScope) this workspace's registry had already flagged. A readiness ratchet whose input is pre-release cannot be left to float — it would stop being a ratchet — but nor can it be left indefinitely: stale, it measures an old question and cannot see new checks. So the currency check is deliberate and dated rather than automatic
deferrals.meanwhile: The pin is exact, so nothing moves under the gate silently; the weekly suite-alpha job exercises the floating alpha tag at the registry's revision, but it does NOT drive the 2026-07-28 scenarios, so it cannot see draft scenario churn — that blind spot is what this row covers

deferrals.what: Re-verify every register row dated 2026-06-09..12 in docs/plan/01-ecosystem-context.md before external use
deferrals.why: The register's own maintenance rule 1: rows older than 90 days must be re-verified before citation
deferrals.meanwhile: Rows carry verification dates; CI does not consume row facts

deferrals.what: Re-decided 2026-06-27 — do NOT file the 'add POST-path resumption' fix. The 2026-07-28 draft removes SSE stream resumability and Last-Event-ID from Streamable HTTP (register 1.5d Major #9, SEP-2575), so that fix is obsoleted by the spec. Re-scoped to the durable residue: assess whether rmcp's hang on early POST-stream close (instead of surfacing a re-issuable error, which the new text REQUIRES) is worth filing — judged against the FINAL spec text plus the draft suite's transport/sse scenarios
deferrals.why: The original premise (2025-11-25 requires the Last-Event-ID resumption rmcp lacks on the POST path) is being deleted by 2026-07-28; filing the add-resumption fix now would ask upstream to build a mechanism the next revision removes, while upstream is already implementing the removal (register 3.11). The re-scoped hang question cannot be verified until the final text ships (2026-07-28) and the draft suite scenarios stabilize
deferrals.meanwhile: Register rows 3.12 + 1.5d carry the reconciliation; the dossier (docs/reports/rmcp-sse-resumption-dossier.md) records that the spec removes the requirement and re-scopes to the hang. The 2025-11-25 mechanism remains exact — re-verified first-hand 2026-06-27 at rmcp head eb435c6 (raw_sse_to_jsonrpc l.303 'without reconnection logic'; POST arms l.778-779/803-804; SseAutoReconnectStream GET-only at l.584/720) — and the reference host still passes sse-retry 3/3, so the evidence is preserved if the decision reopens

deferrals.what: Re-decided 2026-08-18, the review-by having passed on 2026-08-10 — outcome recorded, not re-dated blind. rust-sdk#902 (the everything-server offer, posted 2026-06-11) is still OPEN with ZERO replies at 68 days: no comment, no assignee, no linked PR, labelled P2/enhancement. Next re-decision: re-ping, or record the offer as lapsed in 07-ecosystem-engagement backlog item 1. Posting upstream is a maintainer action (this repo's own pattern, issue #9), so the ledger records the state and the text; it does not post
deferrals.why: R9's trigger is TWO substantive offers unanswered for 60+ days, and only ONE is unanswered. The companion filing of the same day, rust-sdk#903 (enumNames dropped in the ElicitationSchema serde round-trip), was ANSWERED: closed and fixed by PR #905, merged 2026-06-20 — nine days, authored by an outside contributor and approved by a maintainer. So upstream does engage with well-formed filings; what is unanswered is the adoption *offer* specifically, which is a bigger ask than a bug report and sits behind their own SEP-implementation wave. R9 has NOT fired and M4's DoD does not re-scope yet
deferrals.meanwhile: Risk R9 row (trigger restated with the one-of-two count); issue #9 tracks the conversation; the rust-sdk#903 → #905 outcome is the standing evidence that filings land

deferrals.what: Re-decided 2026-08-18, the review-by having passed on 2026-08-15. HALF OF THIS ROW IS NOW BUILT: the draft ratchet DRAFT_SUITE_VERSION moved 0.2.0-alpha.9 → 0.2.0-alpha.11 with a BLESS=1 re-measurement and a scenario diff review in the same commit. What remains deferred is the STABLE pin only — xtask's SUITE_VERSION (0.1.16, the 2025-11-25 gate) — which bumps when a stable 0.2.0 exists, refreshing both expected-failures baselines and the agreement divergence ledger in the same change. The two pins are no longer coupled: 03-conformance-strategy now states their separate triggers, because holding a pre-release ratchet back does not keep its measurement stable, it makes it describe an older question
deferrals.why: There is still nothing stable to bump SUITE_VERSION to: npm `latest` is 0.1.16, published 2026-03-30 and unchanged for four and a half months (re-fetched 2026-08-18). Pin bumps are deliberate PRs with a scenario diff review (03-conformance-strategy §Official-suite version policy). The previous revision of this row claimed the alpha dist-tag had been 'quiet since 2026-07-01'; that was false by the next day — alpha.10 published 2026-07-27 and alpha.11 on 2026-08-07 — which is why this row no longer predicts upstream quiet and states only what was observed
deferrals.meanwhile: Weekly suite-alpha job runs the alpha dist-tag non-blocking at the registry's revision; the draft ratchet now pins alpha.11 and gates every check's status; conformance#338's fix arrives with the stable bump and its agreement-divergence entry will go stale loudly
